stage1/review/A1/v0/Clarity:
Review: The component (segmentation-adapter targets), the supervision (image-level labels on six sources), the pseudo-mask rule and the outcome (fraction of mask-supervised pixel AUROC and Dice recovered) are all named. The pseudo-mask rule leaves its threshold ('no close neighbour') and the feature level it is computed on undefined.
Feedback: State the pseudo-mask rule operationally: which CLIP level, which distance, and how the threshold is chosen without target labels (for example a percentile of normal-to-normal distances on source validation data).
Rating (1-5): 4
stage1/review/A1/v0/Relevance:
Review: Directly addresses G3, the dependence of localisation on dense masks from three datasets, and uses the three image-only BMAD sources that MVFA currently cannot use for localisation. It builds on CoDeGraph's pseudo-mask supervision and the weak-supervision line in the review set.
Feedback: Make the link to G4 explicit only if the same mechanism is also tested in the few-shot setting; otherwise keep the focus on zero-shot source training.
Rating (1-5): 5
stage1/review/A1/v0/Originality:
Review: Pseudo-masks from patch-level nearest-neighbour discrepancy are known (PatchCore-style scoring, CoDeGraph uses batch-level graphs to supervise prompt-driven VLMs), and weakly supervised localisation is a mature area. The new element is the question of whether MVFA's multi-level adapters can be trained this way and what the image-only datasets contribute; that is a useful but moderate step.
Feedback: Sharpen what is new relative to CoDeGraph: for example, that the pseudo-masks come from labelled abnormal images rather than unlabeled batches, so image-level labels can veto false positives.
Rating (1-5): 3
stage1/review/A1/v0/Feasibility:
Review: Pseudo-masks are computed once with frozen features and then replace the mask loader; training cost equals MVFA's. The risk is pseudo-mask quality on low-contrast modalities (ChestXray, HIS), which could make the comparison uninformative.
Feedback: Plan a pseudo-mask quality check on the three masked datasets (pseudo vs true mask IoU) before training, so a negative result can be attributed.
Rating (1-5): 4
stage1/review/A1/v0/Significance:
Review: Removing the need for dense masks would let MVFA use any image-level labelled archive and would show how much expert annotation actually buys; either outcome is informative for clinical adoption.
Feedback: Report results as a label-cost curve (no masks, masks on one dataset, masks on three) to make the significance concrete.
Rating (1-5): 4
